# Voiding Invoices and Re-applying Payments

Sometimes an invoice should never have been raised — it went to the wrong customer, the amount was wrong, or the order was cancelled. OrderHub lets you void it. What it will not do is quietly delete anything: a voided invoice stays on record with its PDF, its number is never reused, and any money that had been applied to it has to be dealt with deliberately before the void goes through.

This article covers voiding an invoice, what to do with payments that were applied to it, and how to put that money somewhere else afterwards.

The Accounts area is reached from **Dashboard → Management → Accounts**.

---

## Two different Void buttons

There is a **Void** button on the **Invoices** tab and another on the **Receipts** tab. They do very different things, so check which tab you are on.

| | **Accounts → Invoices** → Void | **Accounts → Receipts** → Void |
|---|---|---|
| What it voids | The invoice document | The payment you received |
| Effect on money | None — money must be released or moved first | Reverses every allocation on that payment |
| Effect on the customer | They no longer owe against that invoice | The payment is treated as never received |
| Use it when | The invoice was raised in error | The payment itself was recorded in error, or a cheque bounced |

If a customer genuinely paid you and the invoice was simply wrong, you want the **Invoices** tab. Voiding the payment instead would wipe out a payment you actually banked.

---

## Voiding an invoice

### What voiding does and does not do

* The invoice keeps its row, its number and its PDF. Nothing is deleted.
* Its number is never reused. If you need to re-issue, the replacement gets a fresh number.
* The reason you give is stored with it.
* It does **not** cancel the order, and it does **not** refund anybody.

### How to void an invoice

1. Go to **Accounts → Invoices**.
2. Find the invoice. You can use **Search invoice # or order #**, the status filter (**All statuses**, **Open / Unpaid**, **Partial only**, **Paid**, **Voided**), the company filter, or tick **Order cancelled only** to see invoices sitting on cancelled orders.
3. On the invoice's row, click the red **Void** button.
   * Note: the button is hidden on invoices that are already voided.

![Accounts and Invoices](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/987c7a72-59d1-40ec-b22d-af7d8f95cc47.png)

4. The **Void invoice** window opens and immediately checks whether any money is still applied. While it checks you will see *Checking whether any money is still applied…* and the confirm button stays greyed out.
5. Choose a **Reason**: **Created in error**, **Wrong customer**, **Wrong amount**, **Order cancelled**, **Replaced by a new invoice**, or **Other**.
6. Add a **Note (optional)** if it helps the next person understand.
7. Click **Void invoice**.

---

## When money has already been applied

If a payment has been applied to that invoice's order, the void is refused and you will see:

> Money is still applied to this order. Release it back to the payment, or move it to another invoice, first.

![Void invoice already paid](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/d15a7ff2-25a1-4583-8066-8642909e4549.png)

Underneath, every payment still sitting on the order is listed with the amount **Applied**. A payment shows its reference where it has one (a cheque number, for example); cash payments usually have no reference, so they appear as the method and date, such as *Cash · 23 May 2026*.

Two labels are worth knowing:

* **Not linked to an invoice** — that money went onto the order without being tied to a specific invoice. It still counts, which is exactly why it is listed here.
* **from a $100.00 cash payment** — only part of a larger payment was applied to this order. The rest is still sitting on that payment.

You must clear each line before the void will go through. For each one you choose **Release back to payment** or a specific invoice to move it to.

### Release or move — which one?

| | **Release back to payment** | **Move to another invoice** |
|---|---|---|
| What happens | The money comes off this order and goes back to sitting on the payment, unapplied | The money comes straight off this order and onto the invoice you pick |
| Choose it when | You do not yet know where the money belongs | You already know which invoice it should have paid |
| Afterwards | You apply it later from the Receipts tab | Nothing more to do |

**Important:** move and release are alternatives, not steps. Once money has been released you cannot then move it — you re-apply it from the Receipts tab instead (see below). If you already know the destination, moving is the shorter route.

### To release

1. Leave the **Move to** column on **Release back to payment**.
2. Click **Release**.

You will see *Payment released*, and the list refreshes. When every line is clear, the **Void invoice** button becomes available.

### To move

1. In the **Move to** column, pick the destination invoice. The list shows other open invoices for the same company with the amount still due, for example *INV-10175 · $14.98 due*.
2. The button changes to **Move**. Click it.

![Void Payment to another Invoice](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/a2624a1e-b1a1-46e5-884c-ce0e9676b0fd.png)

You will see *Payment moved*. Only invoices belonging to the same company are offered.

* Note: nothing is ever deleted by a release or a move. OrderHub writes a matching reversal line so the original payment, the customer's receipt and the full history all stay intact.

---

## Where released money goes

Released money goes back to the payment it came from, where it sits as **Unapplied**.

To see it, go to **Accounts → Receipts** and click the payment's row. The drill-down shows **Amount**, **Applied** and **Unapplied**, with the unapplied figure highlighted in amber when there is money left over. The **Allocations** list below shows the original line struck through with the release beneath it, labelled *Released* along with the reason given.

![Unapplied Receipts](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/c7bacc1a-2303-443c-9bc8-c509fc380294.png)

* Note: the Receipts list itself does not show an unapplied column, so the only way to spot money sitting unapplied today is to open the payment.

---

## Applying a payment to another invoice

Unapplied money — whether released from a voided invoice, or left over from a payment that was larger than the invoices it was recorded against — can be put onto any open invoice for the same account.

1. Go to **Accounts → Receipts** and click the payment's row.
2. Click **Apply payment**. The button only appears on a payment whose status is **posted** and which has money left over.
3. The **Apply payment** window opens, headed with the account name and a line telling you how much of the payment has not been applied yet.
4. Under **Allocate to invoices** you will see every open invoice for that account: **Invoice / Order**, **Date**, **Due**, **Total**, **Paid**, **Balance** and an **Apply** box.
5. Either type amounts into the **Apply** boxes, or click **Auto-allocate oldest first** to fill them from the oldest invoice down.
6. Watch **Allocated** and **Unapplied** at the bottom. You cannot apply more than the payment has left.
7. Click **Apply payment**.

![Apply Payments](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/f25cd5b3-3db5-4709-baa1-fd256339fb34.png)

The whole lot is applied together. If any line would break a rule — paying an order more than its total, for example — nothing at all is applied and you will be told why. You will never end up with half of it applied.

Invoices that are fully covered move to **paid**; partly covered ones move to **partial**.

* Note: if the account has no open invoices, you will see *No open invoices for this account.* The money stays where it is and can be applied once an invoice is raised for that account.

---

## Good to know

* **Voiding an invoice does not refund anyone.** It withdraws the document. If a customer is genuinely owed money back, that is a refund, handled separately.
* **A voided number is gone for good.** Re-issuing produces a new number, which is what your accountant wants to see.
* **Releasing from the Receipts tab** is also possible: open the payment and click **Release** on an allocation line. You will be asked why. There is no move option there — releasing from the payment always sends the money back to unapplied.
* **Voiding a payment is a browser confirmation, not a window.** On the Receipts tab the **Void** button asks *Void this receipt? Allocations will reverse.* and acts immediately on OK.
* **If a customer has paid more than they will ever be invoiced for**, that money will sit unapplied with nothing to apply it to. Make a note of it against the account so it is not forgotten.
* **Payments applied to invoices never appear on a Z report.** Account payments are recorded against the customer's account, not against a till session, so end-of-day figures are unaffected by anything in this article.
